coverage_claim: Covers identity, classification, managed extent, spatial basis and georeferencing, land basis with planning controls, composition, control and access, lifecycle including temporary construction overlays, hazards and emergency response, measurement and reporting boundary, evidence and interoperability for a managed site or campus. Bounded to the container: legal land units, facility internals, parties, permits-as-instruments and individual assets are referenced by identifier, never re-modelled. No claim of universal completeness across jurisdictions or site types; marine, subsurface and relocatable sites remain an open gap, and alignment to cited standards is declared, not conformance-evidenced.

boundary_decision.rationale: Base (claude) types WM-BLT-008 as an entity; grok types it as an aggregate. A site is a singular governed thing with its own identifier, lifecycle, duty holder, authorisations and record, and it can exist with a single facility or none at all, so aggregation is not constitutive. The COMPLEX / ELEMENT / PARTIAL composition that motivates grok's 'aggregate' reading is a recursive relationship between site instances plus a containment edge to WM-BLT-006, which the entity typing already carries. Typing the model as an aggregate would blur the boundary against the facility model and against reporting-boundary constructs that are also site-shaped collections. Entry kind accepted as entity; grok's composition semantics are absorbed as relationships and a composition function.

add_findings.rationale: Base covers boundary geometry, CRS, vertical datum, positional accuracy and a coarse reference point, but never covers the map conversion that relates a local engineering coordinate system to the real-world CRS, nor the rule that IfcSite RefLatitude/RefLongitude/RefElevation are approximate WGS84 and not a substitute for IfcMapConversion. That is the single most common georeferencing defect in site exchange and is evidence-backed in grok at SRC-001 and SRC-006. It fits the spatial-footprint layer as a sibling of the boundary-geometry finding without restating geometry authoring.

Base has no planning or development-control structure at all: buildable area, site coverage ratio, floor-area ratio, height limit and planned total area are absent, and planning authority is nowhere distinguished from land owner. This is materially missing for a site container, is evidence-backed in grok at SRC-013 (Pset_SiteCommon) and SRC-006 (LandInfra easements, superficie, condominium), and attaches to the land basis alongside the base's existing encumbrance question rather than to operating authorisations.

Base treats construction only as a phase status on part of a permanent site. It has no concept of a time-bounded construction site of the work whose envelope can extend to secondary fabrication and adjacent support sites outside the permanent holding, and no temporary-versus-permanent identity flag. Evidence-backed in grok at SRC-014, SRC-002 and SRC-011 (IsPermanentID). Placed in the lifecycle layer so the temporary overlay cannot silently replace the permanent site identity.

add_functions.rationale: Merge rather than add: the base's define-site-boundary already records geometry, CRS, vertical datum and survey provenance, so grok's georeference-site is folded into it to add the engineering-to-map conversion, site origin and the separation of survey event time from ingestion time, matching the newly added georeferencing finding without creating a near-duplicate operation.

Base carries a full ownership, operatorship, duty-holder and delegation finding but has no function that records or changes those roles; accountability change is only reachable through generic record validation. Adding the role-assignment operation closes an operational gap in the base's own control layer.

Base has parcel and tenure linkage as structure but no operation that binds the site to land units; reconcile-external-site-identifiers targets registries, not cadastre. The function must bind identifiers only, without collapsing legal parcels, consistent with the base's out-of-scope rule for rights, restrictions and responsibilities.

Base can attach a facility and can split or merge sites, but has no operation that sets site-to-site composition (complex, site, section) or records disconnected members of a campus complex. This is a distinct edge type from facility containment and from lineage reorganisation.

Base models contamination and hazard exposure as structure with no operation to attach a contamination or statutory-facility overlay, its affected geometry and its responsible parties. The overlay must be recorded as status, never as a redefinition of the managed extent or of the facility class.

decisions.rationale: Claude states seven neighbour boundaries with explicit distinctions and source refs, separates managed extent from reporting boundary, legal parcel, settlement, utility network and asset-management system, and applies a consistent reference-not-re-model rule. Grok's in-scope list pulls rights, restrictions, responsibilities and planning controls inside while declaring the land-administration object out of scope, which is a less crisp edge. Size was not the deciding factor.

A site holds identity, lifecycle, duty holder and authorisations independent of what it contains, and can contain zero facilities. Composition is modelled as recursive site relationships plus containment edges, so aggregate typing would add no expressive power and would blur the WM-BLT-006 edge.

Base declares CRS and datum but omits the engineering-to-map conversion and the approximate-WGS84 caveat on IfcSite reference latitude and longitude, which is the dominant real-world georeferencing failure and is directly evidenced in IFC 4.3 and LandInfra.

Buildable area, coverage ratio, floor-area ratio and height limit are wholly absent from the base yet are core constraints on a managed land holding, evidenced by Pset_SiteCommon; planning authority is also distinguished from land owner, which the base never does.

decisions.concept: Construction site of the work as a time-bounded overlay
decisions.rationale: The base only has a phase flag on parts of a permanent site. A labour-law or construction envelope can be larger or smaller than the permanent holding and must not be collapsed into it; grok evidences this from 29 CFR 5.2 and IsPermanentID.

decisions.concept: Cadastral SpatialUnitGroup, informal tenure and strata fragmentation
decisions.disposition: rejected as a finding, deferred to research
decisions.rationale: Grok's cadastral-and-land-division-alignment overlaps the base's parcel-and-tenure-linkage on its primary question, and the genuinely novel parts (LADM SpatialUnitGroup grouping, unregistered or customary occupation, condominium and air-right fragmentation) sit on the land-administration side of the base's stated boundary. Deferred rather than duplicated.

A logical enterprise site with no land holding is an alignment target, not a canonical instance of a physical container. The base's standards-alignment-and-system-crosswalks finding already carries alignment targets, mapping loss and matching confidence, and grok itself records no distinctive artifact for this node.

decisions.disposition: rejected as a finding, deferred as a terminology hazard
decisions.rationale: Grok's contamination finding overlaps the base's hazard-exposure finding on contamination status and remediation. Its distinctive value is the warning that a statutory 'facility' is an environmental-liability object that must not be merged into WM-BLT-006; that belongs in boundary guidance and deferred research, and the responsible-party operation is captured by the added record-environmental-status function.

canonical-identifiers and names-and-postal-address restate the base's site-identity-and-designation (master identifier, governed global identifier, Dimension UUID, naming and retirement) and its address questions under external-context-and-connection-points. Land title identifiers remain referenced through the parcel linkage.

Base already asks composition type (complex, site, section), scheme-versioned classification and contiguity with a federation justification. Campus is retained as an operational alias in the scope statement rather than as a competing spatial primitive, consistent with ISO 19650-3 naming campuses without defining a feature type.

decisions.disposition: retained from base, unmatched by grok
decisions.rationale: The rule that an ENERGY STAR parent/child structure or a GHG Protocol organisational boundary may never redefine the managed extent is a load-bearing safeguard present only in the base; without it an agent would corrupt the site definition while compiling a return.

decisions.disposition: retained from base, unmatched by grok
decisions.rationale: SOSA phenomenon-time versus result-time separation grounds the model's temporal discipline for observations and has no counterpart in grok, which treats weather and observation as out of scope.

decisions.disposition: retained from base with regional flag
decisions.rationale: Written plan, evacuation, muster, accounting, alarm and review triggers come from US OSHA 29 CFR 1910.38 and are the only emergency structure either provider produced; the jurisdictional narrowness is carried as a publication hold, not a reason to drop the layer.

compute-site-quantities and publish-interop-mapping are covered by the base's validate-site-record, compile-reporting-boundary and reconcile-external-site-identifiers; the planned-versus-measured area distinction is absorbed into the base's existing quantities finding rather than a new operation.

Both providers place measurement, evidence and interoperability in a single terminal bundle with identical intent, so the service-layer structures are merged into the base's bundle rather than kept as parallel branches.

publication_holds: Source and live-version verification is incomplete: the two providers cite IFC 4.3 from different hosts (ifc43-docs.standards.buildingsmart.org versus standards.buildingsmart.org) and different documentation builds, and grok-sourced Pset_SiteCommon, Pset_LandRegistration and IfcMapConversion claims must be re-fetched and pinned against the single host and version chosen for the base before merge.

Paywalled and blocked sources remain unverified at clause level: ISO catalogue entries (55001, 19650-1, 19650-3, 19152-1, 19152-2, 41011, 6707-1), IEC 62264-1 and the ENERGY STAR campus guide PDF were cited for title, edition and scope only; no clause-level wording may be published as quotation or requirement.

Multi-profile domain validation is not complete: the synthesised model must be exercised against at least three materially different site profiles (for example a university or hospital campus, a process or industrial site, and a port, data-centre or utility holding) before publication, since the evidence pack contains no instance-level validation.

Jurisdictional profile verification is outstanding: emergency planning (29 CFR 1910.38), regulatory site identity (EPA FRS), benchmarking (ENERGY STAR), physical security (NIST SP 800-53), contaminated land (CERCLA/RCRA) and construction wage envelopes (29 CFR 5.2) are all United States instruments; at least one non-US jurisdiction cross-check is required before the model is presented as jurisdiction-neutral.

No governed global location identifier scheme is asserted: GS1 GLN could not be fetched (HTTP 403) and ISO/IEC 81346 reference designation texts are paywalled, so any identifier-grammar claim must stay out of the published draft.
deferred_research: LADM SpatialUnitGroup binding for multi-parcel campuses, plus unregistered, customary and informal occupation, and condominium, strata and air-right fragmentation: decide whether the site model needs an explicit binding pattern or remains a reference to the land-administration sibling model.

Terminology collision between the statutory CERCLA/RCRA 'facility' (any site or area where a hazardous substance has come to be located, or all contiguous land under common control) and the ISO 41011 facility used by WM-BLT-006: an explicit overlay rule is needed so environmental-liability objects are never merged into the facility model or allowed to enlarge the managed extent.

IEC 62264 / ISA-95 role-based site alignment: confirm that a geometry-less logical enterprise site is an alignment target only and cannot satisfy canonical physical-site validation, and record where the enterprise hierarchy is authoritative for rough-cut planning.

Marine, subsurface, offshore and relocatable managed holdings: neither provider located a primary source defining a managed-site container for these cases; the vertical-extent and water-body accommodations are partial and the boundary is unresolved.
Non-US contaminated-land and major-hazard regimes (Seveso, IED, UK COMAH and equivalents) as overlays on the hazard and authorisation structure, to test whether the US-derived structure generalises.
Site-level accessibility requirements and biodiversity or ecological baseline accounting: both appear only as single questions or constraints, with no primary standard cited by either provider.
